spec.description: Manhattan's 22,324 buildings raised to their surveyed roof height and coloured by era, against the MTA subway's lines and stations: how much of the city stands within walking distance of a train. The buildings load once into the browser with their nearest station, and Chaski and Mosaic filter the 3D map, the figures, the station catchments and the charts at once, by distance, height, year, era, station or a drawn area; a timeline plays the city rising since 1719. Data from a public GeoLens catalogue.

options.content:
# Manhattan, by height and by subway

Two open datasets and one question: how much of Manhattan is actually within
walking distance of a train?

The buildings are NYC Open Data's footprints — 22,324 across Lower and Midtown,
each with a surveyed roof height and a year of construction. The subway is the
MTA's own open data: 29 services and 496 stations, with step-free access marked
on each. Neither was downloaded from its publisher: both came through a public
[GeoLens](https://datasets.geolibre.app) catalogue, found by following a shared
GeoLibre project, and are read here from its Parquet exports, through the
gateway's cache.

Three things worth knowing before you read the map:

- **Press play on the timeline.** Every building carries its year, so the
  timeline runs from 1719 to today and the city rises as it plays.
- **The years belong to the lot, not to the tower.** The file's second-tallest
  building, 1,428 ft, is dated 1924 — a year when the tallest thing in New York
  was the 792 ft Woolworth Building. `construction_year` records the earliest
  structure on the site, not the one measured here.
- **The areas here are recomputed.** The file ships a `shape_area` column
  measured in Web Mercator, which at this latitude inflates every area by about
  74 %. Every square metre on this dashboard is measured from the geometry in
  UTM 18N instead.

Everything is filtered in your browser: brush the distance to the nearest station, the
roof height or the years in the filters, pick eras on the chart, draw an area on the map, or
click a station (on the map or in the table) to keep the buildings it is nearest to. The
map, the figures, the table and the charts all follow at once.

spec.rawSql:
-- Every building, from the buildings dataset. The filters (years, distance,
-- height, era, station, drawn area) reach the map as clauses of the Mosaic
-- selection bldgFilters and filter it on the GPU, so this never runs again.
SELECT bin, height_ft, height_m, height_axis, era, construction_year, time, footprint_m2,
       dist_m, station, routes, clat, clng, geom
FROM $buildings

SELECT service, service_name, ST_AsText(geometry) AS geom
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/geolens/datasets/fd3a8635-1f38-4b51-a18f-784ea84abbbf.parquet')

-- The stations; a click on one keeps the buildings it is nearest to.
SELECT station, stop_name, routes, step_free, structure, latitude, longitude FROM $stations

spec.description: Manhattan's buildings extruded to their roof height and coloured by era, with the subway's services and its stations (green step-free, amber partly, grey not). Everything the filters keep stays standing: brush years, distance or height, pick eras, draw an area, or click a station (or a building) to keep the buildings nearest to that station; click empty ground to let go.
spec.title: Every building, raised to its own height

spec.rawSql:
-- Buildings that pass every filter, their footprint and the tallest; and the
-- share within walking distance: within the distance brushed in the filters
-- (400 m with none) among the buildings every other filter leaves.
WITH w AS (
  SELECT coalesce(try_cast($d_lo AS DOUBLE), 0) AS lo, coalesce(try_cast($d_hi AS DOUBLE), 400) AS hi
)
SELECT round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE $__crossfilter($bldgFilters, -dist) AND dist_m BETWEEN w.lo AND w.hi)
             / nullif(count(*) FILTER (WHERE $__crossfilter($bldgFilters, -dist)), 0), 1)::DOUBLE AS "Within reach",
       (count(*) FILTER (WHERE $__crossfilter($bldgFilters)))::DOUBLE AS "Buildings shown",
       round(sum(footprint_m2) FILTER (WHERE $__crossfilter($bldgFilters)) / 10000, 1)::DOUBLE AS "Footprint (ha)",
       max(height_ft) FILTER (WHERE $__crossfilter($bldgFilters))::DOUBLE AS "Tallest (ft)"
FROM $buildings, w
GROUP BY w.lo, w.hi

spec.description: Within reach: the share of the buildings the other filters keep that stand within the distance brushed in the filters, or within 400 m of a station (a five-minute walk) when none is brushed; distances are straight lines from the building's centre to the nearest station. Then the buildings every filter keeps, their footprint in hectares and the tallest.
spec.title: Within walking distance

spec.rawSql:
-- The catchment of every station: the buildings it is the nearest station to,
-- under every filter but the station itself, so the other stations stay
-- listed. The first row clears the pick; a click on a station keeps its
-- catchment. No quotes in these comments: one would hide the macros below.
SELECT '' AS pick, '— All stations —' AS "Station", '' AS "Routes", '' AS "Step-free",
       count(*)::DOUBLE AS "Buildings", round(max(height_ft))::DOUBLE AS "Tallest (ft)",
       round(sum(footprint_m2))::DOUBLE AS "Footprint (m2)", round(median(dist_m))::DOUBLE AS "Median walk (m)", 0 AS o
FROM $buildings
WHERE $__crossfilter($bldgFilters, -station)
UNION ALL
SELECT station, station, any_value(routes), any_value(step_free),
       count(*)::DOUBLE, round(max(height_ft))::DOUBLE, round(sum(footprint_m2))::DOUBLE, round(median(dist_m))::DOUBLE, 1
FROM $buildings
WHERE $__crossfilter($bldgFilters, -station)
GROUP BY station
ORDER BY o, "Buildings" DESC

spec.description: Every station with the buildings it is the nearest station to, under the other filters: how many, the tallest, their footprint and the median straight-line walk. Click a station to keep its catchment on the map and in every chart; the first row lets go.
spec.title: Stations, by the buildings they are nearest to

spec.rawSql:
-- Every era, whatever the era filter says: the chart is where eras are
-- picked, so the ones left out stay on it, in grey, to be clicked back. Every
-- other filter applies.
SELECT era, count(*)::DOUBLE AS buildings, round(avg(height_ft), 1)::DOUBLE AS avg_height_ft
FROM $buildings
WHERE $__crossfilter($bldgFilters, -era)
GROUP BY era
ORDER BY min(coalesce(construction_year, 9999))

spec.description: Buildings standing today by the era of their lot, in the map's colours, with each era's average roof height as a tick. Click a bar to keep only that era; click others to add or remove them. The map, the coverage figure and the station table follow.

spec.description: Manhattan's buildings with their nearest subway station and the distance to it, read by the server once per visit.
spec.name: buildings

query.rawSql:
-- Server side, once per visit: Manhattan's 22,324 building footprints, each with
-- the subway station nearest to its centre and how far that is, in metres, in
-- a straight line, measured in UTM 18N (22,324 buildings against 496 stations,
-- about a second). The browser then filters them by height, year, distance,
-- era, station and drawn area without asking the server again. along_km is how
-- far up the island the building stands, from the Battery along Manhattan's
-- street grid (29 degrees east of north), for the skyline seen from the side.
-- Areas come from the geometry in UTM, not from the file's Web Mercator
-- shape_area, which overstates them by about 74 % at this latitude. Geometry
-- is rounded to 1e-6 degrees (about 10 cm), a third less to load.
WITH s AS (
  SELECT stop_name || ' · ' || daytime_routes AS station, daytime_routes AS routes,
         CASE ada WHEN 1 THEN 'Full' WHEN 2 THEN 'Partial' ELSE 'None' END AS step_free,
         ST_Transform(geometry, 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:32618', always_xy := true) AS pt
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/geolens/datasets/c646ff35-82eb-442f-a524-efcbb1645023.parquet')
),
b AS (
  SELECT bin, height_roof, era, construction_year, geometry,
         ST_Transform(geometry, 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:32618', always_xy := true) AS g
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/geolens/datasets/4a0bd0db-cd92-424a-8a2e-62d270ae918a.parquet')
),
c AS (
  SELECT bin, height_roof, era, construction_year, geometry, ST_Centroid(g) AS pt, ST_Area(g) AS footprint_m2,
         ST_Centroid(geometry) AS c4326
  FROM b
),
near AS (
  SELECT c.bin, arg_min(s.station, ST_Distance(c.pt, s.pt)) AS station,
         arg_min(s.routes, ST_Distance(c.pt, s.pt)) AS routes,
         arg_min(s.step_free, ST_Distance(c.pt, s.pt)) AS step_free,
         min(ST_Distance(c.pt, s.pt)) AS dist_m
  FROM c, s
  GROUP BY c.bin
),
battery AS (
  SELECT ST_Transform(ST_Point(-74.0170, 40.7033), 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:32618', always_xy := true) AS o
)
SELECT c.bin,
       round(c.height_roof, 1)::DOUBLE AS height_ft,
       round(c.height_roof * 0.3048, 1)::DOUBLE AS height_m,
       least(round(c.height_roof, 1), 600)::DOUBLE AS height_axis,
       c.era,
       c.construction_year::DOUBLE AS construction_year,
       -- The timeline's clock. Years before 1600 are the file's way of saying
       -- "no idea": NULL keeps those buildings out of a window, not on one date.
       CASE WHEN c.construction_year >= 1600 THEN make_timestamp(c.construction_year, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0) END AS time,
       round(c.footprint_m2)::DOUBLE AS footprint_m2,
       round(n.dist_m)::DOUBLE AS dist_m,
       n.station, n.routes, n.step_free,
       round(((ST_X(c.pt) - ST_X(battery.o)) * sin(radians(29)) + (ST_Y(c.pt) - ST_Y(battery.o)) * cos(radians(29))) / 1000, 3)::DOUBLE AS along_km,
       round(ST_Y(c.c4326), 6) AS clat, round(ST_X(c.c4326), 6) AS clng,
       ST_AsText(ST_ReducePrecision(c.geometry, 0.000001)) AS geom
FROM c JOIN near AS n USING (bin), battery
ORDER BY time NULLS LAST

spec.description: The MTA's subway stations, read by the server once per visit.
spec.name: stations

query.rawSql:
-- Server side, once per visit: the MTA's 496 subway stations, named by stop and
-- daytime routes (four are called Canal St), as the buildings name their
-- nearest one.
SELECT stop_name || ' · ' || daytime_routes AS station, stop_name, daytime_routes AS routes,
       CASE ada WHEN 1 THEN 'Full' WHEN 2 THEN 'Partial' ELSE 'None' END AS step_free,
       structure,
       ST_Y(ST_Centroid(geometry)) AS latitude,
       ST_X(ST_Centroid(geometry)) AS longitude
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/geolens/datasets/c646ff35-82eb-442f-a524-efcbb1645023.parquet')
